transcript.text: On July 15, 2003, officers from the Kenosha County and Prairie Police Departments in Wisconsin were informed about an escaped convict being transported in Cook County, Illinois. According to news sources, the perpetrator in this video, Wesley Ryan Anderson, who has no known affiliation with the famous director, was being transported as a prisoner who was wanted on a warrant. The transport was conducted by the Park Ridge Police Department, who were on their way to Lake County Jail at 238 in the afternoon. Official reports by the police share that Wesley was acting erratic, and officers had noted that he was able to move his handcuffed wrist from his back to his front. This caused officers to pull over on I-294 at Mile Marker 52. The official report shares they immediately advised dispatch of their location and requested assistance due to Wesley's behavior. The report then shares when officers moved to the backseat to re-secure him and de-escalate his behavior. Wesley broke free from the vehicle. Officers allegedly used a taser, but noted it was ineffective. Wesley then ran across the northbound lanes of traffic and jumped over the concrete barrier median into the southbound lanes. The report goes on to share that Wesley, who is listed as being 6'4 and over 200 pounds, was able to overpower a driver that had stopped. While handcuffed, Wesley took their maroon van. He drove off, effectively escaping the police. Roughly 40 minutes later, Wesley ditched the van and stole a Camaro SS in a residential neighborhood, taking it by physical force. Luckily for the officers, the Camaro was. equipped with OnStar. If you are not aware, OnStar is a network-connected vehicle service that provides additional features, like collecting diagnostics or providing services like remotely locking doors or finding your car's location. OnStar also has the special ability to assist police in high-speed chases as well, since one of the network features allows the company to prevent the vehicle from accelerating too fast and even has the ability to temporarily disable the vehicle entirely, and so through OnStar, officers were able to find the Camaro's location. This time, they were prepared with multiple cruisers from numerous police departments to apprehend Wesley, who had driven roughly 30 miles north out of Illinois and into Wisconsin. In this case, Wesley is facing charges for one count of operating a vehicle without consent, one count of first degree recklessly endangering safety, one count of fleeing in a vehicle as the driver, one count of attempting to disarm a police officer, and two counts of battery or threat against a police officer. After his arrest, a $150,000 cash bond was set. As of posting this video, he has yet to have paid that bond and is currently being held in jail, awaiting trial. He submitted a plea of not guilty on all counts. is not entirely clear is why Wesley was arrested in the first place. Official records and jail documents seem to indicate it was possibly due to four arrest warrants stemming from multiple states. Looking through court records, it appears Wesley has a pattern of failing to pay child support, which could have triggered one of the warrants. Notably, he has passed charges related to domestic abuse and multiple charges related to him shooting and killing his own dog in a friend's house in 2019. These actions caused someone to call the police days later over the incident, where they discovered the dog wrapped in trash bags in his front yard. He shot the dog while other people were in the house, leading to a charge of aggravated cruelty to animals and of reckless discharge of a firearm, which held a possible sentence of up to three years in prison. The outcome of that case is not publicly known due to the case being held in Illinois, and with this current case still going through the system, a verdict or possible sentencing is yet to be determined.
